title: Investigating the influence of machine learning and ensemble techniques in predicting online groceries intention: A case of the Philippines
authors: Gumasing, M. J. J.; Casano, J. L.; Fajardo, A. C.
tldr: A hybrid ML framework combining sentiment analysis and ML classifiers achieved 93 percent accuracy in predicting online grocery purchase intention among Filipino consumers, with ML-based feature extraction outperforming manual approaches by approximately 20 percent.
problem_and_motivation: The Philippine e-commerce sector lacks integrated analytical frameworks that combine sentiment analysis with machine learning for predicting online grocery purchase intention. Existing approaches rely on manual feature extraction and fail to capture nuanced sentiment features from product reviews. There is a need for a scalable pipeline that can process unstructured review text and extract sentiment features while maintaining high prediction accuracy.
approach: Scraped 5,000 product reviews from Shopee and Lazada focusing on Filipino grocery products using web crawling techniques.

Implemented a hybrid ML framework with three phases: sentiment analysis using VADER and TextBlob for lexicon-based sentiment scoring, feature extraction using Word2Vec embedding with ML-based feature selection, and ML-based prediction using eight classification algorithms.
Evaluated classifiers using k-fold cross-validation with k=10 to avoid overfitting and ensure reliable generalization.
Compared hybrid approaches combining manual and ML-based feature extraction with purely manual and purely ML-based approaches.
Validated results against prior work and cross-referenced feature importance scores to ensure methodological robustness.
findings: Hybrid ML-based approaches achieved approximately 93 percent accuracy with Random Forest, Extra Trees, and Decision Tree classifiers.
ML-based feature extraction improved prediction accuracy by approximately 20 percent compared to manual feature extraction alone.
Random Forest and Extra Trees provided the highest accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity at 0.93 and 0.99 respectively.
Sentiment polarity analysis revealed that reviews related to fresh produce, electronics, and beauty products consistently exhibited positive sentiment.
Negative sentiment in grocery reviews was primarily driven by high prices, limited product variety, and concerns about the availability of fresh produce.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a hybrid ML framework that integrates sentiment analysis with machine learning classifiers for predicting online grocery purchase intention in the Philippine context. The key innovation is the demonstration that ML-based feature extraction significantly outperforms manual approaches, with the hybrid pipeline achieving 93 percent accuracy. The framework provides a scalable methodology for processing unstructured product review data and extracting actionable consumer behavior insights from e-commerce platforms.
directly_justifies: Hybrid ML approaches combining sentiment analysis and classification achieve approximately 93 percent accuracy in predicting purchase intention.
ML-based feature extraction outperforms manual extraction by approximately 20 percent.
Sentiment analysis of Filipino grocery reviews reveals key drivers of positive and negative consumer perception.
limits: Single-country focus on the Philippines limits generalizability to other markets.
Training data from only two e-commerce platforms may not represent the full market.
Cross-sectional data capture does not account for temporal changes in consumer preferences.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domains 6.A and 6.B are highly relevant as the paper directly applies predictive modeling to consumer spending behavior. Domain 13.A is medium relevance as the paper discusses training data bias and model robustness. Domains 1-5, 7-12, 14 were considered and rejected: the paper does not address Filipino demographics, budgeting, banking, fraud detection, gambling, trust, debt, savings goals, or synthetic data generation. The paper is focused on spending behavior prediction, not personal finance management.

limitations: Data from Shopee and Lazada may not represent all e-commerce platforms.
Cross-sectional design prevents tracking changes in purchase intention over time.
